59536-captain-lucy-and-lieutenant-bob.title: Lieutenant Bob
59536-captain-lucy-and-lieutenant-bob.creator: Unknown
59536-captain-lucy-and-lieutenant-bob.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "The Major's glasses, if you please, Miss Lucy," said Sergeant Cameron, pausing in the doorway with a bow. Lucy, who had run down-stairs on hearing the bell, smiled a good-morning to the tall, soldierly figure that blocked the sunlit entrance, and went into Major Gordon's study for the forgotten glasses.

arxiv-1907-00291.title: Logarithmic growth of local entropy and total correlations in many-body localized dynamics
arxiv-1907-00291.creator: Fabio Anza, Francesca Pietracaprina, John Goold
arxiv-1907-00291.description: Abstract The characterizing feature of a many-body localized phase is the existence of an extensive set of quasi-local conserved quantities with an exponentially localized support. This structure endows the system with the signature logarithmic in time entanglement growth between spatial partitions. This feature differentiates the phase from Anderson localization, in a non-interacting model.

arxiv-2007-15473.title: From generalized arithmetic means to geodesics to Hamilton dynamics to Bregman divergences
arxiv-2007-15473.creator: Henryk Gzyl
arxiv-2007-15473.description: Abstract Here we examine some connections between the notions of generalized arithmetic means, geodesics, Lagrange-Hamilton dynamics and Bregman divergences. In a previous paper we developed a predictive interpretation of generalized arithmetic means. That work was more probabilistically oriented. Here we take a geometric turn, and see that generalized arithmetic means actually minimize a geodesic distance on ℝ n . {\mathbb{R}}^{n}.

arxiv-2011-12248.title: RanStop: A Hardware-assisted Runtime Crypto-Ransomware Detection Technique Conference: arXiv; ; US
arxiv-2011-12248.creator: Nitin Pundir, Mark Tehranipoor, Fahim Rahman
arxiv-2011-12248.description: Abstract . Among many prevailing malware, crypto-ransomware poses a significant threat as it financially extorts affected users by creating denial of access via unauthorized encryption of their documents as well as holding their documents hostage and financially extorting them. This results in millions of dollars of annual losses of the infected victims worldwide.

arxiv-2012-15255.title: Non-thermal light-assisted resistance collapse in a V 2 O 3 -based Mottronic device
arxiv-2012-15255.creator: A. Ronchi, P. Franceschini, P. Homm, M. Gandolfi, G. Ferrini, S. Pagliara, F. Banfi, M. Menghini, J-.P. Locquet, C. Giannetti
arxiv-2012-15255.description: Abstract The insulator-to-metal transition in Mott insulators is the key mechanism for a novel class of electronic devices, belonging to the Mottronics family. Intense research efforts are currently devoted to the development of specific control protocols, usually based on the application of voltage, strain, pressure and light excitation.

arxiv-2101-03507.title: Radiation signal accompanying the Schwinger effect
arxiv-2101-03507.creator: I. A. Aleksandrov, A. D. Panferov, S. A. Smolyansky
arxiv-2101-03507.description: Abstract The properties of the forced oscillations of electron-positron plasma (EPP) generated from vacuum under the action of a short laser pulse are considered. Calculating the density of the conduction and polarization currents within the quantum kinetic approach, we demonstrate the presence of plasma oscillations at the frequency of the external field and its odd harmonics.

arxiv-2401-03919.title: Red novae, stellar mergers in binary and triple systems, and bipolar nebulae
arxiv-2401-03919.creator: Tomek Kamiński
arxiv-2401-03919.description: Abstract Red novae are transients powered by collisions of non-compact stars. Among their progenitors are systems of evolved subgiants and giants stars. Remnants of such red novae display bipolar structures which have remarkably close characteristics to many post-AGB or pre-PN systems.

arxiv-2403-07412.title: GPU-Accelerated Vecchia Approximations of Gaussian Processes for Geospatial Data using Batched Matrix Computations
arxiv-2403-07412.creator: Qilong Pan 1 , Sameh Abdulah 2 , Marc G. Genton 12 , David E. Keyes 2 , Hatem Ltaief 2 , Ying Sun 12
arxiv-2403-07412.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Qilong Pan 1 , Sameh Abdulah 2 , Marc G. Genton 12 , David E. Keyes 2 , Hatem Ltaief 2 , Ying Sun 12. Gaussian processes (GPs) are commonly used for geospatial analysis, but they suffer from high computational complexity when dealing with massive data.

arxiv-2409-15192.title: The Complexity of Counting Turns in the Line-Based Dial-a-Ride Problem
arxiv-2409-15192.creator: Antonio Lauerbach, Kendra Reiter, Marie Schmidt
arxiv-2409-15192.description: Abstract Dial-a-Ride problems have been proposed to model the challenge to consolidate passenger transportation requests with a fleet of shared vehicles. The line-based Dial-a-Ride Problem ( liDARP ) is a variant where the passengers are transported along a fixed sequence of stops, with the option of taking shortcuts.

arxiv-2503-02380.title: Cosmic Acceleration from Nothing
arxiv-2503-02380.creator: Michael R.R. Good, Eric V. Linder
arxiv-2503-02380.description: Abstract We demonstrate that if the universe started as a vacuum fluctuation rather than from a singular Big Bang state, the universe must have a late-time cosmic acceleration. This is required by a “cosmological sum rule” derived using the Schwarzian form of the Friedmann equations.

arxiv-2507-00562.title: Random walks in a field of soft traps and criticality for the dissipative Abelian Sandpile Model
arxiv-2507-00562.creator: Frank Redig, Ellen Saada, Berend van Tol
arxiv-2507-00562.description: Abstract Motivated by the dissipative abelian sandpile model, we analyze the trajectories of a one-dimensional random walk in a landscape of soft traps. These traps, placed at increasing distances from each other, correspond to dissipative sites in the associated dissipative abelian sandpile model.

arxiv-2605-23933.title: KT4EQG: Personalized Exercise Question Generation via Knowledge Tracing
arxiv-2605-23933.creator: Xinyi Gao, Qiucheng Wu, Lu Ding, Q.Vera Liao, Kaizhi Qian, Ying Xu, Shiyu Chang, Yang Zhang, [0.5em] University of California, Santa Barbara

pmc-10571286.title: Challenges for psychiatric nurses working with non-suicidal self-injury adolescents: a qualitative study
pmc-10571286.creator: Xuting Li, Shiyan Liu, Yusheng Tian, Juan He, Hui Chen, Meng Ning, Zengyu Chen, Jiaxin Yang, Yamin Li, Jiansong Zhou
pmc-10571286.description: BackgroundPsychiatric nurses play a crucial role in treating and supporting adolescents with non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) in China. However, few studies have explored their experiences and challenges.ObjectivesThe aim of this qualitative study was to describe the challenges experienced by psychiatric nurses when working with adolescents having NSSI behaviors.MethodsThis was a descriptive qualitative study using phenomenological approach.

pmc-10729227.title: Protocol for a prospective cohort study on the feasibility of application of nutritional ultrasound in the diagnosis and follow-up of patients with nutritional risk at hospital discharge: study on body composition and function (DRECO)
pmc-10729227.creator: José Manuel García Almeida, Diego Bellido, Daniel De Luis, Germán Guzmán Rolo, Gabriel Olveira
pmc-10729227.description: IntroductionNutritional ultrasound (US) is an emerging technique in clinical nutrition for the morphological and structural study of muscle mass. Currently, all definitions of malnutrition include the measurement of muscle mass; however, there is no single way to assess it. It is necessary to develop new techniques to identify muscle involvement in malnutrition that are valid, standardised, reliable, accurate and profitable.

pmc-10737808.title: PURPOSE IN LIFE ACROSS THE COVID-19 PANDEMIC: THE EFFECTS OF COGNITIVE ABILITY, AGE, AND GENDER
pmc-10737808.creator: Niccole Nelson, Cindy Bergeman
pmc-10737808.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In March of 2020, the World Health Organization declared COVID-19 a pandemic. Almost immediately, 95% of the US population was under stay-at-home orders, resulting in widespread uncertainty about the future, low community engagement, and social isolation. These effects may have been detrimental to maintaining a sense of purpose in life across this period, which has been linked to several health and wellness factors, including cognitive ability.

pmc-11430399.title: Cold-induced degradation of core clock proteins implements temperature compensation in the Arabidopsis circadian clock
pmc-11430399.creator: Akari E. Maeda, Hiromi Matsuo, Tomoaki Muranaka, Norihito Nakamichi
pmc-11430399.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The period of circadian clocks is maintained at close to 24 hours over a broad range of physiological temperatures due to temperature compensation of period length. Here, we show that the quantitative control of the core clock proteins TIMING OF CAB EXPRESSION 1 [TOC1; also known as PSEUDO-RESPONSE REGULATOR 1 (PRR1)] and PRR5 is crucial for temperature compensation in Arabidopsis thaliana. The prr5 toc1 double mutant has a shortened period at higher temperatures, resulting in weak temperature compensation.

pmc-11585617.title: A reference quality, fully annotated diploid genome from a Saudi individual
pmc-11585617.creator: Maxat Kulmanov, Rund Tawfiq, Yang Liu, Hatoon Al Ali, Marwa Abdelhakim, Mohammed Alarawi, Hind Aldakhil, Dana Alhattab, Ebtehal A. Alsolme, Azza Althagafi, Angel Angelov, Salim Bougouffa, Patrick Driguez, Changsook Park, Alexander Putra, Ana M. Reyes-Ramos, Charlotte A. E. Hauser, Ming Sin Cheung, M
pmc-11585617.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We have used multiple sequencing approaches to sequence the genome of a volunteer from Saudi Arabia. We use the resulting data to generate a de novo assembly of the genome, and use different computational approaches to refine the assembly. As a consequence, we provide a contiguous assembly of the complete genome of an individual from Saudi Arabia for all chromosomes except chromosome Y, and label this assembly KSA001.

pmc-11647438.title: Quantitative EEG biomarkers for STXBP1 ‐related disorders
pmc-11647438.creator: Alberto Cossu, Francesca Furia, Jacopo Proietti, Caterina Ancora, Chiara Reale, Francesca Darra, Roberto Previtali, Bernardo Dalla Bernardina, Guido Rubboli, Sandor Beniczky, Rikke S Møller, Gaetano Cantalupo, Elena Gardella
pmc-11647438.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveEEG patterns and quantitative EEG (qEEG) features have been poorly explored in monogenic epilepsies. Herein, we investigate regional differences in EEG frequency composition in patients with STXBP1 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy (STXBP1‐DEE).MethodsWe conducted a retrospective study collecting electroclinical data of patients with STXBP1‐DEE and two control groups of patients with DEEs of different etiologies and typically developing individuals matched for age and sex. We performed a (1) visual EEG assessment, (b) qEEG analysis, and (c) electrical source imaging (ESI).

pmc-11688927.title: ETHNICITY AND WELL-BEING AMONG OLDER IMMIGRANTS IN DIVERSE SOCIOCULTURAL CONTEXTS
pmc-11688927.creator: Daniel W L Lai
pmc-11688927.description: The critical interaction between culture, ethnicity, and social determinants of health is a vital area of study, particularly regarding the unique experiences of ethnocultural minority older adults. The complex intersections of these factors across diverse social landscapes are ripe for investigation to uncover inequalities and inform targeted strategies to reduce the inequalities encountered by these groups.

pmc-12378018.title: Genetic Divergence and Isolation of the Green Sea Turtle (Chelonia mydas) in the Red Sea
pmc-12378018.creator: K. Scott, S. He, R. S. Hardenstine, L. K. Tanabe, H. Barrios‐Garrido, M. P. Jensen, L. Afiq‐Rosli, N. E. Wildermann, C. M. Duarte, J. E. M. Cochran, M. L. Berumen
pmc-12378018.description: The green sea turtle Chelonia mydas is a wide‐ranging marine reptile, inhabiting all the world's tropical and warm‐temperate seas. This global distribution makes delineating population boundaries challenging, and molecular tools like genetic markers are often required to define these limits. The Red Sea hosts ~1500 nesting green turtles, but research in the region is limited.

pmc-12466368.title: Time, Ideologies, and Care: Gendered Patterns of Parental Involvement in the UK and Portugal
pmc-12466368.creator: Mariana Pinho, Inês Lourenço, Marisa Lousada
pmc-12466368.description: This study examines cross-national differences in parental involvement, work hours, and gender ideologies among parents in the UK and Portugal. Findings revealed that UK parents, particularly mothers, reported higher childcare involvement, while Portuguese parents worked more paid hours, reflecting fewer structural childcare constraints.

pmc-12472394.title: Bioactive Plant Peptides: Physicochemical Features, Structure-Function Insights and Mechanism of Action
pmc-12472394.creator: Sara Avilés-Gaxiola, Israel García-Aguiar, Luis Alfonso Jiménez-Ortega, Erick Paul Gutiérrez-Grijalva, José Basilio Heredia, Anne Bialecki, Míchel Frédérich
pmc-12472394.description: Different cultures worldwide have attributed particular healing abilities to various plants for a long time. After decades of studies, research has demonstrated that their bioactivity is associated mainly with the presence of natural products, including short protein fragments known as peptides. These molecules may occur naturally in plants or be generated from plant protein through enzyme hydrolysis.

pmc-12693551.title: Challenges in AVNRT ablation in a patient with previous atrio-pulmonary Fontan surgery: a case report
pmc-12693551.creator: Avinash Jeewooth, Atul Kaushik, Aparna Jaswal, Amitesh Chakravarty, Felix Wiedmann, Boldizsar Kovacs, Inga Voges, Nikesh Jathanna, Deepti Ranganathan
pmc-12693551.description: BackgroundPatients with complex congenital heart defects, such as tricuspid atresia, often require palliative surgical interventions like the Fontan procedure to optimize systemic and pulmonary circulation. While these surgeries improve survival rates, they are associated with long-term complications, including arrhythmias, due to significant anatomical and electrophysiological alterations.

pmc-13230265.title: Host metabolic responses to SARS-CoV-2 and influenza viruses: parallels and contrasts
pmc-13230265.creator: Charles Terra, Olivier Terrier, Audrey Le Gouellec
pmc-13230265.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSARS-CoV-2 and Influenza virus are two major respiratory viruses, responsible for the COVID-19 and the flu respectively. To achieve their replication, these viruses do not merely hijack host cells; they reprogram them, and the host’s metabolism is no exception.Aim of the reviewThis review explores how two major respiratory pathogens, SARS-CoV-2 and influenza virus, manipulate host metabolism to fuel their replication and drive disease.Key scientific concepts of the reviewDespite differences in their genome organization and replication strategies, both viruses disrupt central metabolic pathways,

pmc-13415662.creator: Rodrigo Dalmina Rech, Bernardo dos Santos Pizzatto, Gabriel Antônio Bona, Pâmela dos Santos Zanatta, Rafael da Rosa Ulguim, Ana Paula Gonçalves Mellagi, Fernando Pandolfo Bortolozzo

pmc-13538952.title: Human Pressure Structures Range Contraction and Recovery Potential of the Snow Leopard
pmc-13538952.creator: Erik Joaquín Torres‐Romero, Vincenzo Penteriani, William J. Ripple, James R. Allan, Adrian Treves, Kendall R. Jones, Rodney Jackson
pmc-13538952.description: Human‐driven environmental change is rapidly altering species distributions worldwide, and anthropogenic activities are widely recognized as major drivers of range contraction and population decline. However, how human pressure interacts with other ecological processes to shape spatial patterns of persistence and recovery potential remains less well understood.

pmc-13556736.title: 245. Dopaminergic hyperactivity enhances persistent intracranial self-stimulation with reward delivered at random responses within fixed response blocks
pmc-13556736.creator: S Ide, Y Ikekubo, G R Uhl, I Sora, K Ikeda
pmc-13556736.description: BackgroundBehavioral addictions such as gambling disorder are characterized by persistent engagement in reward-seeking under conditions of uncertainty. One candidate mechanism is a bias toward rewards delivered at unpredictable points within a sequence of actions, even when the total amount of reward is matched to fixed schedules. However, the neurobiological basis of this “randomness preference” remains unclear.

pmc-13582401.title: Motivational climate in school sport and adolescent mental health: a systematic review
pmc-13582401.creator: Yuan Wei, Guan-Nan Lai, Cheng Ji, Xiao-Ming Yang, Chun-Yuan Tie
pmc-13582401.description: BackgroundMotivational climate in school-based physical education and sport represents a potentially modifiable context for adolescent mental health; however, its associations with psychological outcomes have not been systematically synthesised. This review aimed to synthesise evidence on perceived motivational climate and adolescent mental health outcomes in school settings.MethodsDatabases were searched from the inception to May 2026 following PRISMA guidelines.

pmc-13583697.title: The Long road to AI–physician partnership starts with learners: a map for AI in medical education
pmc-13583697.creator: Nikhil Patel, Andre Kumar, Jeffrey Chi, Kevin Keet, John Kugler, Jason Hom, Poonam Hosamani
pmc-13583697.description: Medical students and residents are already using generative artificial intelligence (AI) to draft notes, summarise records and generate differential diagnoses, often informally and without institutional oversight. Adoption has outpaced policy and pedagogical processes, which makes restriction an unrealistic response. The practical question is how to integrate these tools so that clinical skills are not replaced as they are being built.

pmc-13633620.title: Genotype × Year Interaction Dominates Mineral Variation in Berry Fractions of Eight Vitis labrusca Cultivars
pmc-13633620.creator: Besim Karabulut, Yahya Uray, Hüseyin Çelik, Bülent Köse, Cafer Kose, Metin Turan, Ozkan Kaya
pmc-13633620.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The mineral composition of grape berries is shaped simultaneously by genotype and by growing season, yet the relative contribution of each source, and of their interaction, is rarely quantified within a single experimental framework.
